summary: Harker records the morning after the attack. Renfield's death is to be certified as misadventure. The party resolves to keep nothing from Mina, who swears to live though she resolves to die if she endangers others. Van Helsing lays out the day's plan: the Count is bound to his material form until sunset, so the party will sterilise his earth-boxes at Carfax, then search the Piccadilly house, while Godalming and Quincey destroy the boxes at Bermondsey and Mile End. Before they leave, Van Helsing touches a piece of Sacred Wafer to Mina's forehead and it sears a red scar into her flesh. They swear a pledge, sterilise all boxes at Carfax by placing Host on the earth, then reach Piccadilly where a locksmith is hired and the door opened. Eight of nine boxes are found in the dining-room and sanctified. Title deeds, keys and toiletries are found, and Godalming and Quincey leave with the keys.

scenes.title: Council and Mina's resolve
scenes.summary: The party decides Mina must be in full confidence. Mina vows she will die if she becomes a danger; Van Helsing forbids it.
scenes.key_quote: You must not die. You must not die by any hand; but least of all by your own.

scenes.title: Van Helsing's plan of the day
scenes.summary: Explains daylight limits the Count; arranges the locksmith ruse, cabs rather than a heraldic carriage and a split of forces.
scenes.key_quote: He cannot melt into thin air nor disappear through cracks or chinks or crannies. If he go through a doorway, he must open the door like a mortal.

scenes.title: The Wafer burns Mina
scenes.summary: Van Helsing touches the Sacred Wafer to her forehead; it sears a mark like white-hot metal.
scenes.key_quote: it had seared it—had burned into the flesh as though it had been a piece of white-hot metal.

scenes.title: The oath
scenes.summary: All kneel, hold hands and swear to be true to each other and to raise the veil from Mina.
scenes.key_quote: We men pledged ourselves to raise the veil of sorrow from the head of her whom, each in his own way, we loved

scenes.title: Sterilising Carfax
scenes.summary: With screwdriver and wrench Van Helsing opens each earth-box, lays a piece of Host on the soil and screws the lid down.
scenes.key_quote: Thus we defeat him with his own weapon, for we make it more holy still.

scenes.title: Waiting in the Green Park
scenes.location: Green Park opposite the Piccadilly house
scenes.summary: The trio smoke cigars on a bench while Godalming and Morris bring a locksmith.
scenes.key_quote: We sat down on a bench within good view, and began to smoke cigars so as to attract as little attention as possible.

scenes.title: The locksmith
scenes.summary: A workman tries a selection of keys, opens the door, cuts a new key, is paid and leaves unnoticed.
scenes.key_quote: not a soul took the slightest notice of the whole transaction.

scenes.title: Search of the Piccadilly house
scenes.summary: Eight of nine boxes found in the dining-room and sanctified; the Count's effects are examined; keys taken to Bermondsey and Mile End.
scenes.key_quote: Eight boxes only out of the nine, which we sought!

locations.name: Old chapel at Carfax
locations.description: Neglected, dusty chapel in which the large earth-boxes sit.
locations.quote: in the old chapel the great boxes looked just as we had seen them last.

locations.name: Piccadilly house
locations.description: Deserted house among spruce neighbours with steps, a railing with spikes, a hall, a dining-room at the back and a stable at the rear across a stone-flagged yard.
locations.quote: looming up grim and silent in its deserted condition amongst its more lively and spruce-looking neighbours.

locations.name: Green Park
locations.description: Park near Arlington Street with benches in view of the house.
locations.quote: At the corner of Arlington Street our contingent got out and strolled into the Green Park.

locations.name: Asylum grounds and station route
locations.description: Lawn crossed on foot to reach the train; Mina's window visible from the lawn.
locations.quote: in the window of my own room saw Mina.

characters.name: Mina Harker

characters.personality: brave, cheerful in front of others
notable_lines: Because if I find in myself a sign of harm to any that I love, I shall die!
Unclean! Unclean! Even the Almighty shuns my polluted flesh!

objects.quote: The earth smelled musty and close

objects.quote: in each was a portion of the Host.

objects.name: Locksmith's tool basket

objects.quote: a thick-set working man with his rush-woven basket of tools.

objects.name: Cigars

objects.quote: I shall wire to my people to have horses and carriages where they will be most convenient.

vampire_lore.rule: By day the vampire is confined to his earthly form
vampire_lore.detail: Until sunset he cannot melt into air or pass through cracks and must open doors like a mortal.
vampire_lore.quote: Until it sets to-night, that monster must retain whatever form he now has.

vampire_lore.rule: Earth-boxes can be sterilised with the Host
vampire_lore.detail: A piece of Sacred Wafer on the soil makes the box useless to him.
vampire_lore.quote: We must sterilise this earth, so sacred of holy memories

vampire_lore.detail: After heavy feeding the Count sleeps late, giving the party a window.
vampire_lore.quote: last night he banqueted heavily, and will sleep late?

vampire_lore.detail: The Wafer sears Mina's forehead, showing she is tainted.
vampire_lore.quote: it had seared it—had burned into the flesh as though it had been a piece of white-hot metal.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count has many lairs and keeps documents
vampire_lore.detail: He holds deeds, keys and paper at the central Piccadilly house.
vampire_lore.quote: The Count may have many houses which he has bought.

vampire_lore.detail: The Piccadilly house smells like the Carfax chapel.
vampire_lore.quote: It did indeed smell vilely—like the old chapel at Carfax

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire victims develop sharper teeth and thin
vampire_lore.detail: Mina's teeth show prominently; no sharpening yet.
vampire_lore.quote: As yet there was no sign of the teeth growing sharper

vampire_lore.detail: Harker reflects that one vampire meant many through love.
vampire_lore.quote: the holiest love was the recruiting sergeant for their ghastly ranks.

puzzles.name: Entering the empty Piccadilly house
puzzles.setup: No key to a house that is legally someone else's.
puzzles.book_solution: Hire a locksmith in daylight, with a titled gentleman present, so the act looks legitimate. Van Helsing recounts the story of the thief who sold a whole house.
puzzles.game_idea: Social-stealth puzzle: pick the time of day, disguise and cover story to get past police and neighbours without alerting.
puzzles.quote: you go take the lock off a hundred empty house in this your London... and no one will interfere.

puzzles.name: Sterilising the boxes
puzzles.obstacle: Open, sanctify and reseal without the Count noticing.
puzzles.book_solution: Open each lid with screwdriver/wrench, lay a piece of Host on the earth and re-screw, leaving boxes looking undisturbed.
puzzles.game_idea: Timed multi-lair crafting-and-action puzzle: carry enough Host for each box.
puzzles.quote: One by one we treated in the same way each of the great boxes, and left them as we had found them to all appearance

puzzles.name: Assigning forces
puzzles.setup: Three lair sites and a house to search.
puzzles.obstacle: Not enough men; Harker wants to guard Mina.
puzzles.book_solution: Split: two to Walworth/Mile End with cabs, three hold Piccadilly.
puzzles.quote: the two doctors and I should remain there, whilst Lord Godalming and Quincey found the lairs at Walworth and Mile End

crafting.method: Unscrew lid, lay Host on soil, screw lid shut.
crafting.purpose: Deny the Count a resting place.
crafting.quote: Taking from his box a piece of the Sacred Wafer he laid it reverently on the earth, and then shutting down the lid began to screw it home

crafting.method: Locksmith fits a key to the lock while holding the door with his knees.
crafting.quote: he held the door partly open, steadying it with his knees, whilst he fitted a key to the lock.
